03-pelican.name: Halcyon
03-pelican.pitch: Mid-century paperback method (Tschichold's bands, Marber's grid, Facetti's abstract science covers) without the pastiche. Every cover has the same three bands: title on paper, a black level strip, and a flat colour field holding one abstract emblem of the book's mechanism. Field colour is the level (yellow, green, ultramarine), and signal red marks the idea.

06-letterform.name: Codepoint
06-letterform.pitch: One book, one character. Each title gets a single glyph from its own subject (∂ for the maths, σ for neural networks, ≈ for context compaction, QKᵀ for transformers), set monumental and cropped above a fixed rule, with the title hung below like a type-specimen caption. Level is how much ink the cover carries: bare paper, ultramarine, then black.

10-wildcard.name: Some Assembly Required
10-wildcard.pitch: Vizuara is a library for building things, and half its titles end in “from Scratch”, so every book is a model kit. Each emblem is an injection-moulded parts tree (a sprue) built from the book's own mechanism: an H-tree runner feeding 32 GPUs for 5D Parallelism, weights as runners for Neural Networks. Card colour and skill-level pips show level, plastic colour shows series, and kit numbers VZ-001 to VZ-052 make the shelf collectable.

01-grid.name: Figure/Ground
01-grid.pitch: One 12 × 15 module grid, one typeface and three inks for every book. Level picks the ground (paper, signal red, black), so a shelf reads as a gradient of difficulty. Each book stands one figure built from squares, circles and bars on that grid, taken from its own mechanism: a GPT's causal mask, a 5D device mesh, an ODE direction field. A notched bookmark ribbon is the imprint, and its length also encodes level.

04-drafting.name: Drawing Office
04-drafting.pitch: Every book is issued as an engineering drawing of the machine it teaches you to build. The brand lives in the title block: drawing number, level stamped in ink squares, capsules and hours as the extent, units (“Tokens”, “GPUs”), and Vizuara as the issuing office. Each cover uses a different real drafting view (section, isometric, detail, break) on one paper, one graphite and one engineering-red ink.

05-algorithmic.name: Figure 0
05-algorithmic.pitch: Every cover is one run of the book's own algorithm, computed in the page from a seed. Gradient descent draws the maths book, a network trained in the browser draws Neural Networks, and a simulated pipeline schedule draws 5D Parallelism. The FIG. 0 caption states exactly what ran, with numbers read back from that run. Ground darkens with level: paper, signal red, carbon.

07-riso.name: Overprint
07-riso.pitch: Every book looks pulled off a risograph: natural paper, two or three real riso inks that overprint, halftone screens made in code, and drums slightly out of register. The idea usually lives where the inks cross: the overprint is the GEMM output tile, the SQL join, the part of the context the model actually sees. Level is a ski-run mark (circle, square, diamond) in the key ink.

09-atlas.name: Interchange
09-atlas.pitch: Each book is a Beck/Vignelli transit map of its own subject. Its parts are the lines and each capsule is one tick, checked against the real capsule counts, so the 69-capsule DSA book coils into a long spiral while the 9-capsule book is tiny. The key at the foot doubles as a table of contents. Beginner and intermediate books are pale day maps, advanced books are dark night maps.

02-plates.name: Specimen Plates
02-plates.pitch: Every book is a numbered plate in one atlas of machine learning: a single engraved specimen of its actual mechanism, lettered a, b, c with an italic legend, the way Gray or Haeckel documented theirs. The drawings are computed, not decorated (descent paths integrated on the real surface, the real 2⁵ device mesh). Paper tone gives level: sage, Ingres blue, sanguine. Everything prints as one spot tint plus black.

13-miniature.name: Muraqqa
13-miniature.pitch: Every cover is a folio from one Mughal album (a muraqqa) with its page architecture held fixed. The coloured margin (hashiya) and the number of gold, vermilion and black rules (jadval) give the level, and a lobed cartouche carries the title. The central miniature is a flat, jewel-toned diagram of the book's real mechanism, such as the causal mask, the 5D device mesh or the paged KV cache, painted in the Basohli manner. A shamsa rosette is the imprint.

17-optical.name: Interference
17-optical.pitch: Every book is one field of black lines plus one spot colour, and the book's own idea is the force that bends them: a Gaussian swells them, a causal mask turns them, compaction squeezes them, attention makes two ring systems interfere. At 180px each field averages into one bold emblem; in the hand it shimmers. Line pitch gives level: coarse for beginner, fine for advanced.

16-wit.name: Double Take
16-wit.pitch: One idea per book: a single flat-shape pun, metaphor or figure–ground trick you get in a second, and each has to be technically true. Context engineering is the mark that reads B across and 13 down; a spider spins a neural net; a retriever fetches a document for RAG; trees are drawn upside down, the way computer scientists draw them. One typeface, and three grounds (newsprint, red, black) that give level.

21-wildcard2.name: Some Assembly Required II
21-wildcard2.pitch: A second designer, told nothing about direction 10, independently arrived at the same idea: every Vizuara book builds a model, so every cover is a model kit. This take is more pictorial. The book's real components are moulded as pictograms on a sprue, numbered in build order, and laid on a cutting mat ruled in true inches. Plastic colour names the field, Skill 1/2/3 squares give level, and the Charlie books are a gold-plated Factory Edition.

22-open.name: Textmode (open brief)
22-open.pitch: This designer was told only who Vizuara is and that the current covers are disliked. It chose to draw every cover in text: each picture is set in a monospaced font on a strict 120 × 74 character grid, like line-printer computer art, showing the real mechanism with real numbers (the causal attention matrix, 32 GPUs labelled with their mesh coordinates, the iris decision tree). A big Fraunces title leads. Colour family marks the subject and lightness marks the level.

11-kolam.name: Pulli
11-kolam.pitch: Every book gets a Tamil sikku kolam computed from the book itself. There is one dot (pulli) per capsule, laid out in the shape of the subject, and a single line weaves around them under the real kolam rules (45° runs, turns at the borders, never touching a dot, always closing). A real mirror-curve engine finds the turns: 5D Parallelism closes as five lines, Pi vs Hermes vs Codex as three. The ground gives level: ink on notebook paper, rice flour on red-oxide kaavi, rice flour on dark earth.

19-terminal.name: stdout
19-terminal.pitch: Every cover is what the book's own code prints. The top two-thirds is a full-bleed field of machine output on a 120 × 80 character grid (an attention matrix, a hex dump, a device mesh, a packed context window) that forms the emblem at arm's length and is real numbers up close. Tone comes from glyph weight, like a line printer. The title is typed at a prompt: > for beginner, $ for intermediate, # (root) for advanced.

14-bombay.name: Signboard
14-bombay.pitch: Every book is lettered like a Bombay shop board and labelled like a Sivakasi matchbox. The title is set in Board Block, a display alphabet built in SVG for this system (coal keyline, split cream-over-chrome fill, red inline, block shadow), widened or narrowed to fill the board as sign-painters do. A matchbox label carries one object from the book's mechanism. Board colour marks the shelf, a perforated stamp marks level, and the imprint runs in Latin and Devanagari at equal size, as Maharashtra's shop-sign rule requires.

20-cutpaper.name: Paperworks
20-cutpaper.pitch: Every book is a small construction of cut, folded and layered coloured card, and the construction is the idea: a die-cut window over a scroll of context, neurons pinned with brass paper fasteners, chat history pleated into a concertina. Board colour marks the subject shelf (Matisse's cut-out palette plus kraft), and the number of sheets stacked under the title slip is the level. In print the layers become real die-cut, laminated board.

08-clothbound.name: Buckram
08-clothbound.pitch: Every book is designed as a real case-bound hardcover: a deep bookcloth, one foil (gold, copper, palladium or black pigment) and one blind die. The title is blocked in Cormorant capitals, and a sunk roundel holds a device from the book's mechanism (a causal attention matrix, the 5-cube in Petrie projection, ⋈ for SQL). A blind-pressed band repeats the subject as pattern. Level is read from the binding itself: quarter-bound, half-bound or full cloth.
